question: This is a topographic map of a real place (Breakneck Ridge, New York), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. Rescue carry: a stretcher team carries a casualty along the Aspen Trail (solid magenta line) from the magenta square S to the magenta square E. To pace the carry, the team leader logs every contour line the trail crosses. How many contour lines (index contours included) does the trail cross between S and E? Neither square stands on a contour line, so count only the crossings between the two squares. If the trail crosses the same contour line more than once, count every crossing. Answer with a whole number, for example 7.
references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (US Topo, 1:24 000): brown contours, heavy index contours
Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP, public domain) via AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (terrarium, zoom 13)

question: This is a topographic map of a real place (Breakneck Ridge, New York), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. A lost hiker at the magenta square S must reach the hut at the magenta square H along the Juniper Trail (solid magenta line) before dark. The incident box on the map gives the time now, the time of sunset and the walking time for the trail's length on flat ground. By Naismith's rule the climb adds time: add 4 minutes for every contour line the trail crosses going uphill (each one is 20 m of climb, at 300 m of climb per hour). Contour lines crossed going downhill add no time, and neither square stands on a contour line. How many minutes before sunset does the hiker reach the hut? Give a negative number if the hiker arrives after sunset. Answer with a whole number of minutes, for example 12 or -7.
references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (US Topo, 1:24 000): brown contours, heavy index contours

Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP, public domain) via AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (terrarium, zoom 13); Naismith's rule for walking time (1892): 1 hour per 4 km plus 1 hour per 300 m of climb

question: This is a topographic map of a real place (Bear Mountain, New York), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. Flash flood: the dam at the magenta square D has failed. The water runs downhill from D, always in the direction of steepest descent, so its path crosses every contour line at a right angle. 6 campsites are marked with magenta points, C1 to C6, all lower than the dam. Exactly one of them lies in the water's path. Which campsite does the water reach? Answer with the campsite name, for example C2.
references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (US Topo, 1:24 000): brown contours, heavy index contours
Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP, public domain) via AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (terrarium, zoom 13); surface water runs down the line of steepest descent, at right angles to the contours
